# FLX-3510: an object store target does not name a usable bucket and prefix

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

The Parquet, Arrow IPC and Delta sinks take an object store URL (s3://, gs://, az:// or abfs://) as their target: the host is the bucket or container and the path is the prefix the files or tables go under, as in parquet:s3://bucket/simulations/run-a. Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 also has its standard form, abfs://CONTAINER@ACCOUNT.dfs.core.windows.net/PREFIX (az:// takes it too), where the part before the @ is the container and the account is the first label of a host that ends in .dfs.core.windows.net; a host with no container before it is refused. The path is split on / and refused when it is empty, or when a segment is empty, . or .., or holds a backslash or a percent-encoded /, \ or . (%2F, %5C, %2E, in either case), so that no spelling of a target can write outside the prefix it shows. The Iceberg sink's catalogue name and each level of its namespace are held to the same rules. A trailing / is allowed and dropped. Every object's key is the prefix, a /, and the relative name a local target would use, and is checked to start with the prefix and a / before anything is written. Name the bucket and a plain prefix; nothing was written.

## Look it up offline

```console
$ fluxsim explain FLX-3510
```
